headline: Blind date: ‘Would we meet again? We’ve swapped numbers … ’
standfirst: Lucy, 40, a general manager, meets Leon, 45, an operations manager at a food charity
trailText: Lucy, 40, a general manager, meets Leon, 45, an operations manager at a food charity
body:
Leon on Lucy

What were you hoping for?
I’m a regular reader and have always wanted to be in the column, so mostly here for the vibes. Bumping into the love of my life would be nice, though …

First impressions?
Enthusiastic and chatty. Australian.

What did you talk about?
Australia. Jobs. Clubbing. Psychology. Politics. Film. Gender. Economics.

Most awkward moment?
There were no awkward moments – except, I suppose, wondering if my gag gift of a toy bat (“as blind as a bat” for a blind date) would land. Hopefully Lucy will find it a fun souvenir.

Good table manners?
We shared all the food. I will not say “impeccable” – a terrible stock answer.

Best thing about Lucy?
Her zest for life.

Would you introduce Lucy to your friends?
I have a broad range of friends who are all pretty chill and friendly, and Lucy is great, so of course! She would certainly fit in with my clubbing crowd!

Describe Lucy in three words
Talkative, fun, interesting.

What do you think Lucy made of you?
I think she had a good time. I hope she thought I was engaging, open and a bit random (in a good way). And interested in her.

Did you go on somewhere?
We went to a couple of pubs, and continued putting the world to rights.

And … did you kiss?
Yes.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
It ended a bit early, as I had to get the coach home.

Marks out of 10?
9. I don’t give 10s – it’s a principle.

Would you meet again?
It was a fun evening. We’ve swapped numbers, and we hang out in some of the same places …

Lucy on Leon

What were you hoping for?
A fun date, a new connection and someone cool to hang out with.

First impressions?
He seemed really kind and genuinely happy to see me, which was lovely.

What did you talk about?
Family. Relationships. Work. Music. It was one of those dates where you end up discussing lots of different topics.

Most awkward moment?
Leon gave me a plastic bat (as in the mammal). I didn’t get the joke and thought he’d brought me a Halloween present, which I found pretty strange.

Good table manners?
He served my aubergine parmigiana, which was very gentlemanly.

Best thing about Leon?
He clearly put effort into planning the date. He’d thought of another pub we could go to if things were going well. It was nice that he’d considered what I might enjoy without knowing me yet.

Would you introduce Leon to your friends?
Yes. He’s friendly and easy to talk to.

Related: Blind date: ‘We overstayed our welcome – the waiters were shaking the cutlery drawer really loudly’

Describe Leon in three words
Thoughtful, outdoorsy, open-hearted.

What do you think Leon made of you?
That I’m fun, chatty and confident.

Did you go on somewhere?
We did! We went to two different pubs.

And … did you kiss?
Yes, we did.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I’d make it summer and start in the day, so we could spend some time outside.

Marks out of 10?
8.7. A fun evening.

Would you meet again?
I’d be open to seeing what happens!

Lucy and Leon ate at Rossella, London NW5. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘I told her I don’t like the theatre. In retrospect, I can see why a playwright would be offended’
standfirst: William, 28, a PhD candidate, meets Abigail, 24, a theatre artist
trailText: William, 28, a PhD candidate, meets Abigail, 24, a theatre artist
body:
William on Abigail

What were you hoping for?
To have a spark of some kind.

First impressions?
She looked very glamorous and suited the smart restaurant far more than I did.

What did you talk about?
Our love of Robert Pattinson. The play she’s working on. Shucking oysters. She asked lots of questions, so I’m worried I dominated. She did a palm reading on me too and it said I’m not a good writer.

Most awkward moment?
When I told her I don’t like theatre. In retrospect, I can see why a playwright and actor would be offended by that.

Good table manners?
I’m gonna go for “impeccable”. She was very friendly and chatty to the staff too.

Best thing about Abigail?
She has a lovely smile and a great sense of humour. I laughed a lot.

Would you introduce Abigail to your friends?
Lots of my friends are performers, so they would have loads to talk about.

Describe Abigail in three words
Funny, kind-hearted, genuine.

What do you think Abigail made of you?
I hope she thought I was kind and easy to talk to. I realised I wasn’t making much eye contact at one point, so “awkward” may be a safer bet. Funny would be a lovely addition.

Did you go on somewhere?
We stayed at the restaurant until closing. Then she walked me back to King’s Cross so I could catch a train back to Cambridge, which was very kind.

And … did you kiss?
I would never say.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I forgot the bathroom was a push door and thought I had locked myself in.

Marks out of 10?
9/10.

Would you meet again?
We’ve shared numbers.

Abigail on William

What were you hoping for?
Love, obviously.

First impressions?
Polite, gentle. Nervous in a sweet way. He was very concerned about being underdressed, but he looked lovely.

What did you talk about?
Standup comedy. Socialism. Academia. His disdain for contemporary British theatre and my adoration of it.

Most awkward moment?
He seemed keen to show off his American accent at a few points.

Good table manners?
Yes, knows his way round a wine list too!

Best thing about William?
He has lived a fantastically varied life of travels and extracurriculars. It’s good to meet people who have life by the horns.

Would you introduce William to your friends?
I’d consider it. But he said he loves lying to strangers. That gives a woman pause.

Related: Blind date: ‘Most awkward moment? When I accidentally called her Melissa’

Describe William in three words
Charming, roguish, amiable.

What do you think William made of you?
I gave him a flirty palm reading and I’m worried he thinks I’ve got a hand fetish.

Did you go on somewhere?
I don’t kiss and tell …

And … did you kiss?
… see above.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I would have stolen his gorgeous thick-rimmed emerald green glasses.

Marks out of 10?
7/10.

Would you meet again?
I fear his love line looked a bit unsteady. But he’s got my phone number if he’d like to tempt fate.

Abigail and William ate at Kobe, London W1. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘He said: “If heaven is real, you’ll definitely be going there”, which might be the nicest thing anyone’s ever said to me’
standfirst: Nelson, 41, who works in legal services, meets Louise, 37, who works in marketing
trailText: Nelson, 41, who works in legal services, meets Louise, 37, who works in marketing
body:
Nelson on Louise

What were you hoping for?
Great company and wonderful conversation.

First impressions?
Louise is such a sweet, sincere person. With very interesting hobbies!

What did you talk about?
All sorts of funny things, from feeding monkeys to the worst theatre shows and wooden toys.

Most awkward moment?
When we met, I wanted to greet her with a friendly hug but she was seated and had to get up.

Good table manners?
Impeccable, and she had amazing taco-eating skills.

Best thing about Louise?
She will laugh and think I’m taking the mick but I’m not: her dedication to the things she loves. So admirable! Passion and commitment. It’s infectious.

Would you introduce Louise to your friends?
Yes.

Describe Louise in three words
Energetic, passionate, excellent conversationalist (four I know!).

What do you think Louise made of you?
An oddball with similar interests?

Did you go on somewhere?
It was a work night so we remained sensible.

And … did you kiss?
It was a work night.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I wouldn’t change a thing! It was a very pleasant date overall.

Marks out of 10?
9 out of 10. A really pleasant evening!

Would you meet again?
Yes, I would.

Louise on Nelson

What were you hoping for?
Fun conversation with an interesting person and to discover a new restaurant.

First impressions?
A gentleman, very polite, laughs very loudly (in a good way).

What did you talk about?
London zoo volunteering – a typical day. Nelson growing up in Singapore. Covid – how I was in Singapore and Bali just as it started kicking off. Theatre shows we’ve been to – how perfect Oliver! is (this was mainly me). How we both go and see all the Oscar-nominated films every awards season. Nelson’s new startup.

Most awkward moment?
The waitress thought a photographer would be joining us and we needed a table for three.

Good table manners?
I was more conscious of my own, as I ate the tacos with my hands while he used cutlery.

Best thing about Nelson?
He’s a very interesting and interested person – so many hobbies and passions. I liked that he shared my enthusiasm for all things cultural.

Would you introduce Nelson to your friends?
Can’t think why not, he’s very interesting and sweet!

Related: Blind date: ‘Most awkward moment? When she squished an insect that was on my forehead’

Describe Nelson in three words
Perceptive, warm, bright.

What do you think Nelson made of you?
He said: “If heaven is real, you’ll definitely be going there”, which might just be the nicest thing anyone’s ever said to me. He also laughed very heartily all the way through so hopefully he thought I was funny.

Did you go on somewhere?
No, but we were the last to leave on a Tuesday night, so pretty good going.

And … Did you kiss?
No.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
The pineapple/lime/cinnamon ice-cream was incredible, we should’ve got one each.

Marks out of 10?
8 (the date, not Nelson as a person!).

Would you meet again?
I think as friends – maybe at the cinema as Oscar season is approaching!

Nelson and Louise ate at Mirtala, London W4. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘We overstayed our welcome – the waiters were shaking the cutlery drawer really loudly’
standfirst: Alexandrea, 32, a lawyer, meets Pardis, 32, a doctor
trailText: Alexandrea, 32, a lawyer, meets Pardis, 32, a doctor
body:
Alexandrea on Pardis

What were you hoping for?
A fun date and to hopefully meet the one!

First impressions?
Handsome and relaxed.

What did you talk about?
The sports we do. Books. Family. Friends. Our jobs. Travelling and travelling mishaps. Vermin infestations. Stocks and shares. ISAs.

Most awkward moment?
We both arrived at the restaurant on time but there was a big queue which resulted in me sitting at the table alone for about 10 minutes – I got a bit nervous.

Good table manners?
No faux pas so all good.

Best thing about Pardis?
He is very sincere. He asked lots of questions, seemed interested in what I was saying and was a great listener. I also loved how laid-back he was – he went with the flow when I proposed the tasting menu.

Would you introduce Pardis to your friends?
Of course – he’s interesting and really good company.

Describe Pardis in three words
Easygoing, kind, engaging.

What do you think Pardis made of you?
A ray of sunshine, akin to what everyone else thinks of me!

Did you go on somewhere?
No, but we did overstay our welcome at the restaurant, to the point where the waiters were shaking the cutlery drawer really loudly.

And … did you kiss?
A lady never tells … But no.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I would have loved it to be in Paris. Pardis in Paris!

Marks out of 10?
8.

Would you meet again?
Pardis is a lovely guy but I think we’re better suited as friends.

Pardis on Alexandrea

What were you hoping for?
The scene in About Time where the protagonist meets Rachel McAdams in that dark dining restaurant. (I appreciate that isn’t quite the same concept as a blind date.)

First impressions?
I was a few places behind her in the queue to get in the restaurant. I could only see the back of her head but thought: nice hair, good fashion sense.

What did you talk about?
There was a healthy amount of chat on the life cycle of a fly and the declining quality of mousetraps. We’ve both had minor pest issues recently – a perk of living in London.

Most awkward moment?
Probably mistaking her Irish accent for a Scottish one. Not my finest hour.

Good table manners?
Excellent, a picture of sophistication.

Best thing about Alexandrea?
Very down to earth, clearly adventurous and a great dinner party guest.

Would you introduce Alexandrea to your friends?
I wouldn’t put the poor girl through the trauma of meeting my rabble …

Related: Blind date: ‘He asked if my disco ball tattoo was an onion’

Describe Alexandrea in three words
Adventurous, kind, intelligent.

What do you think she made of you?
I think she enjoyed my chat. Either that or she’s great at acting entertained (or I’m completely oblivious).

Did you go on somewhere?
No, I was on early morning uncle duty the next day, so had to call it a night.

And … did you kiss?
No, a good wholesome hug.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I’d brush up on my accent recognition beforehand.

Marks out of 10?
8 (for a friendship connection, otherwise it would have been higher).

Would you meet again?
Sure, as friends I’d be happy to.

Alexandrea and Pardis ate at Mildreds, London W1. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘Most awkward moment? When I accidentally called her Melissa’
standfirst: James, 34, a researcher, meets Michelle, 30, a radio presenter
trailText: James, 34, a researcher, meets Michelle, 30, a radio presenter
body:
James on Michelle

What were you hoping for?
An unforgettable evening.

First impressions?
Glamorous.

What did you talk about?
Birmingham, as we both went to university there, but at different times and came away with contrasting perceptions! Food, with a particular focus on madeleines. Reality TV. Music. Comedy. Dancing. Football.

Most awkward moment?
Embarrassingly, I accidentally called her Melissa. (Sorry!)

Good table manners?
Yes – despite Michelle asking me to try her steak tartare, even though I’d mentioned that I was a vegetarian.

Best thing about Michelle?
Easy-going and forgiving (after my slip-up with her name).

Would you introduce Michelle to your friends?
Yeah. She’s easy to get along with.

Describe Michelle in three words
Chilled, creative, bougie.

What do you think Michelle made of you?
Chatty and mildly funny (a couple of my jokes didn’t quite land).

Did you go on somewhere?
Nope, it was a Tuesday night, and past my bedtime.

And … did you kiss?
I don’t kiss on a first date.

If you could change one thing about the date what would it be?
The time: it was in the evening after work, and I was pretty tired. Also, the timing meant I missed the Champions League games on TV that night.

Marks out of 10?
7.5.

Would you meet again?
We’re plotting our next outing.

Michelle on James

What were you hoping for?
To meet someone genuinely interesting who could hold a great conversation.

First impressions?
He came across as incredibly warm and had a relaxed energy, which immediately put me at ease.

What did you talk about?
Our mutual love for discovering great music – it was brilliant to delve deep with someone who appreciates it just as much as I do.

Most awkward moment?
There were none, except at the end of the date when one of my heels broke off.

Good table manners?
Absolutely.

Best thing about James?
He is wonderfully articulate, which made for a really engaging and thoughtful conversation.

Would you introduce James to your friends?
I think he’d get on really well with them.

Describe James in three words
Vibrant, smart, ambitious.

What do you think James made of you?
I’d like to think he found me to be bubbly, fun and naturally gregarious.

Related: Blind date: ‘I do wish I hadn’t stepped on that dog – but she assured me it was OK’

Did you go on somewhere?
No, we just stayed at the restaurant for the evening.

And … did you kiss?
No, we didn’t.

If you could change one thing about the date what would it be?
I’d definitely swap out my footwear!

Marks out of 10?
7.

Would you meet again?
Yes.

Michelle and James ate at Duchy, London EC2. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘Most awkward moment? When she squished an insect that was on my forehead’
standfirst: Holly, 42, a horticulturist, meets Graeme, 47, a forest manager
trailText: Holly, 42, a horticulturist, meets Graeme, 47, a forest manager
body:
Graeme on Holly

What were you hoping for?
Really, just a fun night with minimal awkwardness was my fairly low expectation before the meeting.

First impressions?
A very positive, engaging lady with a beautiful smile.

What did you talk about?
Growing food, the joys of seeds, birdwatching, the failings of young people when it comes to proper raving, epigenetics and breaking generational cycles.

Most awkward moment?
Holly destroying an aphid, which had landed on my forehead, with a firm thumb squish. I should make clear that the poor aphid wasn’t in the lovely restaurant; it was outside an entirely different place, which had hanging baskets.

Good table manners?
Impeccable.

Best thing about Holly?
Holly was incredibly easy to converse with. Her assured nature and wide range of interests meant she was a joy to be with.

Would you introduce Holly to your friends?
In a heartbeat.

Describe Holly in three words
Nuanced, sparkling, niche.

What do you think Holly made of you?
I reckon she was hugely impressed I could name every species of bird she had tattooed on her leg.

Did you go on somewhere?
Yes, a nearby pub then a little nightclub.

And … did you kiss?
Yes, we did.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I would tone down my oversharing

Marks out of 10?
9.8.

Would you meet again?
I’m hugely looking forward to doing so.

Holly on Graeme

What were you hoping for?
To meet someone interesting and fun.

First impressions?
Warm, confident. Graeme quickly made me feel at ease.

What did you talk about?
Our mutual nerves about the evening. The joys of working outside. Forestry management for biodiversity. Rural living. The importance of dancing.

Most awkward moment?
I got overexcited about the menu and ordered quite a lot of food. We didn’t need the extra salad.

Good table manners?
Excellent: he kept our glasses topped up and was open to sharing dishes.

Best thing about Graeme?
He’s got a very curious mind and is a great listener.

Would you introduce Graeme to your friends?
He’d get along well with them.

Describe Graeme in three words
Warm, intelligent, open.

Related: Blind date: ‘We talked about how I don’t like Clapham gays – guess where he lives?’

What do you think Graeme made of you?
I hope he thought I was easy to talk to.

Did you go on somewhere?
We did. We made the most of being in the city and sought out some music and dancing!

And … did you kiss?
Yes.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
Nothing – I had a really fun evening. Graeme is a lovely guy who is very easy to talk to and up for a laugh.

Marks out of 10?
A solid 8.

Would you meet again?
We live quite far apart, but we’ll see …

Holly and Graeme ate at the Palmerston in Edinburgh. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘He asked if my disco ball tattoo was an onion’
standfirst: Shahar, 29, a graphic designer and music label manager, meets Stephen, 34, a product designer
trailText: Shahar, 29, a graphic designer and music label manager, meets Stephen, 34, a product designer
body:
Shahar on Stephen

What were you hoping for?
I’d never been on a blind date, so a good story, and a new connection.

First impressions?
Kind, a bit nervous. Very engaged, but kind of in awe of the situation.

What did you talk about?
Our careers in design. Music. What we like to cook. Artwork and posters we own. His extensive cap collection. Films (lots of movies I need to add to my watchlist).

Most awkward moment?
He asked me if my disco ball tattoo was an onion.

Good table manners?
Excellent. At one point, talking to the waiter, he referred to me as “the lady”, which we had a good laugh about.

Best thing about Stephen?
He was really engaged, easy to talk to, made me laugh – and very generous with compliments. He’s good at leading the conversation, but also at recollecting details and circling back.

Would you introduce Stephen to your friends?
After a while, yeah. It’s quite a compliment, introducing someone to your circle – gotta earn that trust!

Describe Stephen in three words
Thoughtful, authentic, curious.

What do you think he made of you?
I hope he thought I was funny. I did make him laugh quite a few times.

Did you go on somewhere?
We spent four hours over dinner and it was a Sunday, so we called it a night.

And … did you kiss?
We did not.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I wish I’d come across as slightly more curious and not drawn a blank about recent albums I liked. Also, I wish I’d had more room to finish dessert!

Marks out of 10?
8 (8.5 really, but I’m honouring Stephen’s dislike of .5 ratings).

Would you meet again?
We did chat about maybe going to a gig or the cinema.

Stephen on Shahar

What were you hoping for?
Some cute flirting with someone my judgmental female friends would approve of.

First impressions?
Gorgeous hair, an American accent.

What did you talk about?
We compared graphics, recent albums, films and cinema etiquette. Then moved on to how fancy the venue was, our favourite things to cook, the perils of dating apps and the lost art of flirting.

Most awkward moment?
Nothing major. I did refer to Shahar as “the lady”, but only because the place was so fancy!

Good table manners?
Perfect, nothing spilled, many well-shared drinks and plates.

Best thing about Shahar?
I admired her passion and approach to design – and again, great hair!

Would you introduce Shahar to your friends?
I reckon they’d yap up a storm.

Related: Blind date: ‘He probably thinks I hold a lot of strong opinions on frivolous matters’

Describe Shahar in three words
Elegant, chatty, curly.

What do you think she made of you?
A film nerd with a large hat collection.

Did you go on somewhere?
I suggested another drink, but it was too late. To be fair, we did stay at the restaurant for almost five hours.

And … did you kiss?
The vibe didn’t lend itself to kissing, and that’s OK; there was lots to take in.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
Our seats being so far apart and not meeting on a school night.

Marks out of 10?
8 for the date. I couldn’t judge a person like that.

Would you meet again?
I gave her my number, so let’s see. There are lots of gigs and films we could watch.

Shahar and Stephen ate at Cooper’s Cut, London EC3. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘I do wish I hadn’t stepped on that dog – but she assured me it was OK’
standfirst: Miklos, 25, a PhD student, meets Minnie, 23, who works in film production
trailText: Miklos, 25, a PhD student, meets Minnie, 23, who works in film production
body:
Miklos on Minnie

What were you hoping for?
To take a step outside my comfort zone. To meet the love of my life.

First impressions?
Confident, and just as confused as I was about how to start off a blind date.

What did you talk about?
The optimal time horizon to plan your life ahead – we oscillated between one and 10 years. After that, I’m embarrassed to admit, loads of K-pop.

Most awkward moment?
On my way to the loo I stepped on a dog by accident. I felt horrible, but Minnie assured me it was OK.

Good table manners?
The food was so intimidatingly tasty it forced the best table manners out of us. Hers were almost too good, I’d say.

Best thing about Minnie?
She is from the best part of town (in my opinion) and it shows. She is unabashedly herself.

Would you introduce Minnie to your friends?
They love a bottle of wine. She loves a bottle of wine. There is nothing more to say.

Describe Minnie in three words
Talkative. Fuzzy. Edgy.

What do you think Minnie made of you?
I think she saw me quite accurately: nerdy, but willing to push boundaries and have some fun.

Did you go on somewhere?
We did not.

And ... did you kiss?
No kissing was had.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I wish I had not stepped on that dog – that’s it really.

Marks out of 10?
9.

Would you meet again?
By the end of the date, it was clear to both of us that we were missing a romantic spark … That’s life!

Minnie on Miklos

What were you hoping for?
A fun evening.

First impressions?
Very lovely guy, good vibes. I was a tad late and he was super understanding. He also noted that he often goes by Mickey, which is pretty funny.

What did you talk about?
Travel. Studies. Controversial opinions on music concerts. Katseye (sorry, Miklos).

Most awkward moment?
Neither of us could figure out the menu.

Good table manners?
Yes, very polite.

Best thing about Miklos?
He is super different from me. It was nice chatting with someone who has lived such a different life.

Would you introduce Miklos to your friends?
Hypothetically yes, but only as a friend.

Related: Blind date: ‘Bizarrely, she suddenly realised she knew my daughter’

Describe Miklos in three words
Intelligent, chatty, inquisitive.

What do you think Miklos made of you?
That I was easy to talk to.

Did you go on somewhere?
Nope, just headed home.

And ... did you kiss?
Couple of hugs, not the vibe for a kiss.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
We both said we would have liked to have been in a different part of town by the canal (the restaurant was lovely though).

Marks out of 10?
7.

Would you meet again?
Probably not, but no hard feelings.

Miklos and Minnie ate at the Bull and Last, London NW5. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘We talked about how I don’t like Clapham gays – guess where he lives?’
standfirst: David (left), 34, a children’s doctor, meets Dec, 31, a culture and sex writer
trailText: David (left), 34, a children’s doctor, meets Dec, 31, a culture and sex writer
body:
Dec on Dave

What were you hoping for?
A sweet-hearted madman who would make me belly laugh.

First impressions?
Looked like a David. A bit nervous and jittery, but considerate, curious and chatty (all the best C-words).

What did you talk about?
People in cars shouting “ginge” at him. Us coming from the West Country (but only I sound like it). How I don’t like Clapham gays – guess where he lives?

Most awkward moment?
I tried on his stethoscope, pretending to listen for a heartbeat from the chicken.

Good table manners?
Sound as a pound.

Best thing about David?
His passion for his profession. Also, how he was so keen to ask, listen and hear.

Would you introduce David to your friends?
Possibly, so they can give him his second Buzzballz ever!

Describe David in three words
Moustached, kind, grounded.

What do you think David made of you?
Probably an absolute loony. No, I wonder if he saw through the tarty humour to my kind, smart, caring self.

Did you go on somewhere?
The kitchen was closing, and he had to work in the morning, saving lives – very inconsiderate.

And … did you kiss?
I gave him a polite peck on the cheek when we hugged bye-bye.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
Nothing: it was the perfect balance of sincere connection and nonsense.

Marks out of 10?
A solid 6. He’s a cracking bloke and rocks a floral shirt better than anyone I know. It’s a 6 not a 7 because I don’t like fish or salad; he kindly ordered me both.

Would you meet again?
We swapped numbers. We’re not each other’s “spark”, but had a good evening.

David on Dec

What were you hoping for?
Someone who put me at ease, asked me questions and made me want to text my friends about him in the toilet.

First impressions?
Definitely a main character. Handsome, potty-mouthed, charming and equally clueless about tapas.

What did you talk about?
Dec’s love of swearing. Coming out.

Most awkward moment?
Possibly when I realised I had a child’s blood on my trousers.

Good table manners?
Impeccable.

Best thing about Dec?
He’s very free and at ease in himself, and made me feel I could be too. And his autobiography will be a bestseller.

Would you introduce Dec to your friends?
I would. But I didn’t toilet-text them.

Describe Dec in three words
Curious, beautiful, free.

What do you think Dec made of you?
Hopefully good company! “Doctor” brings a whole set of expectations, but it felt like he was able to see past all that.

Related: Blind date: ‘Would we meet again? Stay tuned, divas’

Did you go on somewhere?
We didn’t – but we stayed until closing.

And … did you kiss?
A quick peck at the station.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
We were side-by-side at the bar, which is weird for a first date. And he got my right side, which is definitely less good.

Marks out of 10?
8.

Would you meet again?
We agreed the chemistry felt more friendly than romantic, but I’d love to stay in touch.

Dec and David ate at Barrafina Drury Lane, London WC2. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘He probably thinks I hold a lot of strong opinions on frivolous matters’
standfirst: Joe, 27, who works in advocacy at a charity, meets Jade, 29, a PR account manager
trailText: Joe, 27, works in advocacy at a charity, and meets Jade, 29, a PR account manager
body:
Joe on Jade

What were you hoping for?
Human connection outside an algorithm – good conversation and a fun anecdote.

First impressions?
Jade was friendly and the conversation flowed easily from the get-go.

What did you talk about?
Favourite Doctor Who episodes (The Girl in the Fireplace, obviously). The joys of London in the summer. Favourite gig venues. The need for the transatlantic accent to return.

Most awkward moment?
A slight disagreement about whether the BT Tower is evil – I begged to differ.

Good table manners?
Impeccable from my end.

Best thing about Jade?
She has a clear sense of what she wants in life. And excellent chat.

Would you introduce Jade to your friends?
Sure thing.

Describe Jade in three words.
Open, enthusiastic, fun.

What do you think Jade made of you?
Probably too many gesticulations, but otherwise, hopefully, normal enough.

Did you go on somewhere?
No, she had an early flight, but we made a pretty good dent in the Guardian’s tab at the restaurant!

And … did you kiss?
No, merely a hug on the Mildmay line on the way home.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
It was a lovely evening, so no complaints here.

Marks out of 10?
8.

Would you meet again?
We have exchanged numbers!

Jade on Joe

What were you hoping for?
To make a connection with someone and have a good story to tell our future pets.

First impressions?
Cute and well dressed.

What did you talk about?
Books. Family pets. Our favourite parks in London. The housing crisis. The constant yearning to be by the sea when you grew up by the coast. Debating whether it’s better to be a reality TV villain or completely erased from the final cut for being too boring.

Most awkward moment?
We got right into chatting and I wasn’t prepared when they came to take our order – so had to ask for extra time.

Good table manners?
He kept my water glass full and humoured my plan to say cheers with every new drink.

Best thing about Joe?
He was really fun to talk to. We were on the same wavelength on a lot of things, but it was also fun to discuss when we weren’t.

Would you introduce Joe to your friends?
I would.

Describe Joe in three words.
Intelligent, thoughtful, affable.

What do you think Joe made of you?
Probably that I’m very talkative and hold a lot of strong opinions on frivolous matters.

Related: Blind date: ‘She’s one of the easiest people to talk to that I’ve ever met’

Did you go on somewhere?
I had to catch an early flight the next morning, so we parted ways on the Overground.

And … did you kiss?
Just a hug goodbye.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
I would have enjoyed staying out a bit later – I doubt it would have made my 5am start the next day much harder.

Marks out of 10?
9.

Would you meet again?
Yeah! We’re in touch about planning our next outing.

Joe and Jade ate at the Bull & Last, London NW5. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

Favourite gig venues. The need for the transatlantic accent to return. Most awkward moment? A slight disagreement about whether the BT Tower is evil – I begged to differ. Good table manners? Impeccable from my end. Best thing about Jade? She has a clear sense of what she wants in life. And excellent chat. Would you introduce Jade to your friends? Sure thing. Describe Jade in three words. Open, enthusiastic, fun. What do you think Jade made of you? Probably too many gesticulations, but otherwise, hopefully, normal enough. Did you go on somewhere? No, she had an early flight, but we made a pretty good dent in the Guardian’s tab at the restaurant! And … did you kiss? No, merely a hug on the Mildmay line on the way home. If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be? It was a lovely evening, so no complaints here. Marks out of 10? 8. Would you meet again? We have exchanged numbers! Jade on Joe What were you hoping for? To make a connection with someone and have a good story to tell our future pets. First impressions? Cute and well dressed. What did you talk about? Books. Family pets. Our favourite parks in London. The housing crisis. The constant yearning to be by the sea when you grew up by the coast. Debating whether it’s better to be a reality TV villain or completely erased from the final cut for being too boring. Most awkward moment? We got right into chatting and I wasn’t prepared when they came to take our order – so had to ask for extra time. Good table manners? He kept my water glass full and humoured my plan to say cheers with every new drink. Best thing about Joe? He was really fun to talk to. We were on the same wavelength on a lot of things, but it was also fun to discuss when we weren’t. Would you introduce Joe to your friends? I would. Describe Joe in three words. Intelligent, thoughtful, affable. What do you think Joe made of you? Probably that I’m very talkative and hold a lot of strong opinions on frivolous matters. Did you go on somewhere? I had to catch an early flight the next morning, so we parted ways on the Overground. And … did you kiss? Just a hug goodbye. If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be? I would have enjoyed staying out a bit later – I doubt it would have made my 5am start the next day much harder. Marks out of 10? 9. Would you meet again? Yeah! We’re in touch about planning our next outing. Joe and Jade ate at the Bull & Last, London NW5. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘Bizarrely, she suddenly realised she knew my daughter’
standfirst: Don, 76, who works in TV and film, meets Claire, 63, a counselling charity manager
trailText: Don, 76, who works in TV and film, meets Claire, 63, a counselling charity manager
body:
Don on Claire

What were you hoping for?
To meet someone interesting. To be part of a cultural phenomenon called the Guardian Blind date. To have a pleasant lunch.

First impressions?
Relaxed and friendly.

What did you talk about?
Family. Work. Alcohol. Catholicism. Buddhism … and other light topics!

Most awkward moment?
I didn’t feel any. Bizarrely though, Claire suddenly realised she knew one of my daughters, and her sister was a good friend of my mother a long time ago. Scotland is a small but beautiful nation.

Good table manners?
I have the worst table manners north of the border, so I couldn’t comment.

Best thing about Claire?
Very easy to have a conversation with. Freckly arms! A good human being.

Would you introduce Claire to your friends?
Yes, I have a disparate group of friends and most of them would like her company.

Describe Claire in three words
Thoughtful, empathetic, compassionate.

What do you think she made of you?
Haven’t a clue. That’s for her to answer.

Did you go on somewhere?
We walked to the bus stop.

And … did you kiss?
In a European kind of way.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
That I had not had to drive to the railway station and so could have had a glass of cold white rioja.

Marks out of 10?
8.

Would you meet again?
Hopefully. Not sure we’ll run away to Gretna Green, but maybe see a film, or go for a walk or a meal.

Claire on Don

What were you hoping for?
Good company and conversation.

First impressions?
Warm and friendly face.

What did you talk about?
His film script and past experiences as a producer and documentary-maker. My work as a counsellor. Meditation. Movies. Our kids and marriages. How bloody awful Trump is.

Most awkward moment?
Not really awkward for us, but the restaurant owner thought we were here for Dining across the divide, and when we said it was Blind date he was a bit thrown and very apologetic.

Good table manners?
No issue as far as I was concerned.

Best thing about Don?
Easy to talk with and asked interested questions.

Would you introduce Don to your friends?
Turns out he knows a fair few already.

Describe Don in three words
Bon vivant, warm and interesting.

What do you think he made of you?
That I am friendly, interesting and easy to talk with.

Related: Blind date: ‘I got the impression he liked me well enough, but who knows?’

Did you go on somewhere?
No, it was lunchtime so it was back to work for me.

And … did you kiss?
A continental farewell.

If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be?
An evening rather than lunch meet-up.

Marks out of 10?
8 – he was great company.

Would you meet again?
I need a spark and it wasn’t there for me. But numbers were exchanged –plenty more conversation to be had.

Claire and Don ate at Tapa, Edinburgh. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘She’s one of the easiest people to talk to that I’ve ever met’
standfirst: Mike, 37, a scientific editor, meets Caterina, 35, a teacher
trailText: Mike, 37, a scientific editor, meets Caterina, 35, a teacher
body:
Mike on Caterina

What were you hoping for?
Good company, nice food and an interesting evening with someone new. I got everything I hoped for.

First impressions?
Warm, confident and easy to talk to.

What did you talk about?
The joys of being an aunt/uncle. Freelance life. Jury duty as a newly minted British citizen.

Most awkward moment?
None that I recall, so either the evening went smoothly or the malbec did its job.

Good table manners?
If there were any faux pas, I was too busy enjoying the conversation to notice.

Best thing about Caterina?
She’s genuinely one of the easiest people to talk to that I’ve ever met.

Would you introduce Caterina to your friends?
Without hesitation.

Describe Caterina in three words
Warm, kind, elegant.

What do you think Caterina made of you?
Hopefully polite, easy company and good for a chat. Perhaps a lack of shared passions meant the spark wasn’t there, but the conversation never ran dry.

Did you go on somewhere?
We were the last two in the restaurant, so we went for a stroll around London until midnight, when I had to dash for the last train back to Cambridge.

And … did you kiss?
Sorry to disappoint: just a farewell hug.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
I’d have liked a bit more time before that last train forced the evening to end.

Marks out of 10?
9.5. Hard to fault a thoroughly enjoyable evening just because it wasn’t heading toward romance.

Would you meet again?
We may meet for a coffee when I’m in London, and there’s an open invitation for a guided tour of Cambridge.

Caterina on Mike

What were you hoping for?
To meet someone special.

First impressions?
Nice smile and face; a bit nervous or shy.

What did you talk about?
Favourite cuisine. Past and future travels. Harry Potter. Even politics.

Most awkward moment?
I felt I was leading the conversation most of the time, asking questions.

Good table manners?
Very nice: he would pour water in my glass whenever it was empty.

Best thing about Mike?
You can tell he’s someone who loves putting care into what he does and what he says – a rare find these days.

Would you introduce Mike to your friends?
Not sure – my friendship group has a lot of energy.

Describe Mike in three words
Organised, thorough, kind.

Related: Blind date: ‘I asked him to compliment my outfit and he said he didn’t really like it’

What do you think Mike made of you?
Not sure. Maybe that I’m a weird woman who eats fast and laughs loudly!

Did you go on somewhere?
We had a walk around Soho/Covent Garden – I felt he deserved a bit of tourism, coming from Cambridge.

And … did you kiss?
No, just a hug.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
Nothing major – maybe just a slightly quieter spot to chat.

Marks out of 10?
7.5.

Would you meet again?
As friends. I would like to grab a coffee together.

Mike and Caterina ate at Tagine & Grill at the Sun and 13 Cantons, London W1. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘There was a mature, polite peck on departure at a busy Manchester Piccadilly station’
standfirst: Susan, 74, a retired careers adviser, meets Pete, 72, a retired Methodist minister
trailText: Susan, 74, a retired careers adviser, meets Pete, 72, a retired Methodist minister
body:
Susan on Pete

What were you hoping for?
A relaxed, friendly lunch with good and fun conversation.

First impressions
Pete was immediately welcoming and relaxed. I felt at ease pretty quickly.

What did you talk about?
An awful lot! Our optimism around our new PM. There was a good deal of common ground, including that I had twins, while he was a twin, and we both fall asleep at night listening to Radio 4 podcasts!

Most awkward moment?
There weren’t really any, except perhaps my revelation that I didn’t eat red meat … but that didn’t prove to be a problem.

Good table manners?
Impeccable.

Best thing about Pete?
His obvious kindness and sociability. His clear ability to have put his thoughts and beliefs into positive, meaningful action.

Describe Pete in three words?
Humanitarian, genuine, interesting.

Would you introduce Pete to your friends?
No reason why not – but to be honest, my family would be more important. He is very easy to get on with.

What do you think Pete made of you?
Well, I guess I will find that out here!

Did you go on somewhere?
No.

And … did you kiss?
A mature, polite peck on departure at a busy Manchester Piccadilly station.

If you could change one thing about the afternoon what would it be?
There were areas of conversation I would have liked to have gone a bit deeper, but it didn’t seem the occasion to do so.

Marks out of 10?
For a lunchtime out in excellent company and meeting my hopes, a very strong 8.

Would you meet again?
We exchanged numbers but there was no romantic spark … and I think my agnosticism would be a sticking point.

Pete on Susan

What were you hoping for?
At the least, an interesting afternoon … possibly more.

First impressions?
Susan has a lovely smile.

What did you talk about?
What didn’t we talk about? Walking in the Peak District. Running half marathons. Family. A little about religion. The Labour party. Sailing. Cancer … the time went so quickly.

Most awkward moment?
Perhaps after getting the menu and noting that Susan is pescatarian.

Good table manners?
Very. We shared most of the lovely dishes brought for us.

Best thing about Susan?
She is very easy to talk with.

Describe Susan in three words?
Fascinating, attractive, lovely.

Would you introduce Susan to your friends?
Yes. She would get on well.

What do you think Susan made of you?
Someone who has travelled a lot – and perhaps talks too much.

Did you go on somewhere?
Only a walk back to the railway station together.

Related: Blind date: ‘I got the impression he liked me well enough, but who knows?’

And … did you kiss?
No. There was no spark of that kind.

If you could change one thing about the afternoon what would it be?
Not much. I had excellent company and great food. We were the last to leave the restaurant.

Marks out of 10?
8.5.

Would you meet again?
If I were in the areas of the Peak District we both know and love, we might go for a walk.

Susan and Pete ate at Stow in Manchester. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘I got the impression he liked me well enough, but who knows?’
standfirst: Andrew, 75, a retired graphic designer, meets Gilli, 64, a counsellor
trailText: Andrew, 75, is a retired graphic designer / cartographer and meets Gilli, 64, is a training consultant, group facilitator and counsellor
body:
Andrew on Gilli

What were you hoping for?
An exciting evening in a great restaurant with a lovely lady I might be able to start a relationship with.

First impressions?
Gilli looked absolutely fantastic, with lovely curly hair.

What did you talk about?
The usual … Life history and relationships. The difference between acquaintances and friends. Where we are in life. Music. Hobbies. U3A groups. No politics.

Most awkward moment?
Perhaps me choosing oysters for my starter.

Good table manners?
Excellent. And we both chose healthy meals – no grills for us. And no alcohol as we were both driving.

Best thing about Gilli?
Her beauty, and her enthusiastic and confident conversation.

Would you introduce Gilli to your friends?
Definitely.

Describe Gilli in three words
Vivacious, loquacious and beautiful.

What do you think Gilli made of you?
I really don’t know, though I hope she found me smiley, chatty, confident and humorous. But perhaps she thought I was too old?

Did you go on somewhere?
She said she was tired and didn’t want to go to another venue. Manchester was buzzing, so that was a shame.

And ... did you kiss?
Two pecks on the lips!

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
An earlier start so we could have had more time – it flew by.

Marks out of 10?
9.

Would you meet again?
We discussed meeting again (and swapped numbers), but the age gap and different desires for the future make another date pointless.

Gilli on Andrew

What were you hoping for?
A warm, interesting connection with friendship or relationship potential.

First impressions?
A confident, happy and lively person. Andrew didn’t seem at all nervous, so it was relaxed from the get-go.

What did you talk about?
Our careers. Life paths. Travel and where we’ve both lived. Food.

Most awkward moment?
I was shattered, so really could not stay out late. I sensed Andrew was a bit disappointed that I needed to get home.

Good table manners?
I didn’t notice anything untoward.

Best thing about Andrew?
He is an interesting and engaging person who likes to live life to the full. He has interesting ideas for his life going forwards.

Would you introduce Andrew to your friends?
He likes to go dancing, as do my friends and I, so he’d go well with them.

Describe Andrew in three words
Engaging, lively and happy.

Related: Blind date: ‘We were chatting as soon as we sat down’

What do you think Andrew made of you?
I got the impression he liked me well enough, but who knows?

Did you go on somewhere?
Andrew walked me to my car.

And … did you kiss?
We had a goodbye peck.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
I would have preferred a lunchtime meet-up as we could have gone on to a gallery or somewhere and made a day of it.

Marks out of 10?
9.

Would you meet again?
We may meet up to do arty things but we both knew there wasn’t any relationship potential due to the age gap and different life stages.

Andrew and Gilli ate at Grand Pacific in Manchester. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘I asked him to compliment my outfit and he said he didn’t really like it’
standfirst: Imogen, 31, a doctor, meets Andy, 36, founder of a consultancy firm
trailText: Imogen, 31, a doctor, meets Andy, 36, founder of a consultancy firm
body:
Imogen on Andy

What were you hoping for?
Something to tell the group chat that would elicit more :o reactions than usual.

First impressions?
Polite, nice hands, early.

What did you talk about?
We covered most of the world’s topics, my favourite being whether having an AI boyfriend is functionally the same as being in a long-distance relationship (I admit that was slight rage bait).

Most awkward moment?
I jokingly asked for a compliment on my outfit and he said he didn’t really like it. I told him white lies exist for a reason …

Good table manners?
Excellent – my water glass was never empty and our food was always perfectly shared down the middle. (By the way, best roast of my life.)

Best thing about Andy?
An unparalleled debate partner who called me out when he disagreed with me (which I appreciated).

Would you introduce Andy to your friends?
My single ones would love him.

Describe Andy in three words
Witty, self-aware, circumspect.

What do you think Andy made of you?
He swore he wasn’t, but I felt as if he might have been a bit overwhelmed by me – especially when I asked what his dream wedding would look like.

Did you go on somewhere?
We went to the pub, then threw sticks for his dog Bella in the park (11/10 for her).

And … did you kiss?
Cheek only.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
Make it 5C cooler so I didn’t have to fan myself like an aghast Victorian maiden.

Marks out of 10?
6.6.

Would you meet again?
To debate, or to dog-walk.

Andy on Imogen

What were you hoping for?
To be able to say, “You’ll never guess how we met.”

First impressions?
What a whirlwind.

What did you talk about?
Living abroad and learning languages. Tarot cards. The joy of dancing. The insufficiency of men. Autism.

Most awkward moment?
When Imogen asked why I hadn’t complimented her outfit.

Good table manners?
Flawless – glasses were attended at all times, swear words used only at appropriate points, all waiting staff were treated with admiration.

Best thing about Imogen?
Her openness and love of all things strange and interesting.

Would you introduce Imogen to your friends?
Yes.

Describe Imogen in three words
Charismatic, intelligent, direct.

Related: Blind date: ‘We were chatting as soon as we sat down’

What do you think Imogen made of you?
She told me I was a nerd, and we related in our passion for various things novel and brave – so an adventurous nerd?

Did you go on somewhere?
We did – to a pub, and then for a walk.

And … did you kiss?
On the cheek.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
I’d have complimented her outfit.

Marks out of 10?
8.

Would you meet again?
I think Imogen could probably make anything a party, so yes.

Imogen and Andy ate at Wilson’s, London, SE13. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

Most awkward moment? I jokingly asked for a compliment on my outfit and he said he didn’t really like it. I told him white lies exist for a reason … Good table manners? Excellent – my water glass was never empty and our food was always perfectly shared down the middle. (By the way, best roast of my life.) Best thing about Andy? An unparalleled debate partner who called me out when he disagreed with me (which I appreciated). Would you introduce Andy to your friends? My single ones would love him. Describe Andy in three words Witty, self-aware, circumspect. What do you think Andy made of you? He swore he wasn’t, but I felt as if he might have been a bit overwhelmed by me – especially when I asked what his dream wedding would look like. Did you go on somewhere? We went to the pub, then threw sticks for his dog Bella in the park (11/10 for her). And … did you kiss? Cheek only. If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be? To be able to say, “You’ll never guess how we met.” First impressions? What a whirlwind. What did you talk about? Living abroad and learning languages. Tarot cards. The joy of dancing. The insufficiency of men. Autism. Most awkward moment? When Imogen asked why I hadn’t complimented her outfit. Good table manners? Flawless – glasses were attended at all times, swear words used only at appropriate points, all waiting staff were treated with admiration. Best thing about Imogen? Her openness and love of all things strange and interesting. Would you introduce Imogen to your friends? Yes. Describe Imogen in three words Charismatic, intelligent, direct. What do you think Imogen made of you? She told me I was a nerd, and we related in our passion for various things novel and brave – so an adventurous nerd? Did you go on somewhere? We did – to a pub, and then for a walk. And … did you kiss? On the cheek. If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be? I’d have complimented her outfit. Marks out of 10? 8. Would you meet again? I think Imogen could probably make anything a party, so yes. Imogen and Andy ate at Wilson’s, London, SE13. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘I joked we should join the young people for a club night. We didn’t’
standfirst: Richard, 63, a communications consultant, meets Katrina, 60, a GP
trailText: Richard, 63, a communications consultant, meets Katrina, 60, a GP
body:
Richard on Katrina

What were you hoping for?
Easy conversation with someone interesting, smart and relaxed.

First impressions?
Katrina arrived and my blind date trepidation vanished. She looked good, was warm, and the conversation flowed straight away.

What did you talk about?
Our grownup kids. Running. Travel. Our devotion to our coffee machines.

Most awkward moment?
I thought Katrina was still working her way through her post-meal mint tea, so was taken aback when she said, “Shall we call it a night?”

Good table manners?
Impeccable.

Best thing about Katrina?
She is great company.

Would you introduce Katrina to your friends?
Yes. I’m sure she gets on really well with most people.

Describe Katrina in three words
Calm, warm, open.

What do you think Katrina made of you?
She laughed at a few things I said, and we had quite a few things in common, so I think she felt I was easy company.

Did you go on somewhere?
As we left the restaurant and saw a queue of young people outside a bar, I joked that we should join them for a club night. We didn’t.

And … did you kiss?
No.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
Nothing. I had a fun evening with a lovely woman and don’t think it could have been improved.

Marks out of 10?
A strong 8.

Would you meet again?
I really enjoyed Katrina’s company, we talked and laughed a lot. So of course.

Katrina on Richard

What were you hoping for?
To finally meet “the one”.

First impressions?
Polite, relaxed and quietly handsome.

What did you talk about?
Coffee snobbery – our coffee machines (identical), the best beans, our children aspiring to own the same machine.

Most awkward moment?
Arriving late.

Good table manners?
Impeccable. Attentive without ever being overbearing.

Best thing about Richard?
He’s a great conversationalist.

Would you introduce Richard to your friends?
Of course.

Describe Richard in three words
Warm, genuine, polite.

What do you think Richard made of you?
I hope he saw me as warm, approachable and engaging.

Did you go on somewhere?
No. We looked at the club opposite, but agreed that wasn’t going to happen.

Related: Blind date: ‘I should have made a move, but I’m not good at that sort of thing’

And … did you kiss?
No. Just a polite and rather formal goodbye.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
Honestly, not much. I really enjoyed the evening, and for a blind date it exceeded my expectations.

Marks out of 10?
9/10.

Would you meet again?
Possibly, as friends – I’m not sure there was a romantic spark, but I really enjoyed his company. I’d happily introduce him to the joys of the hill at Ashton Court parkrun.

Katrina and Richard ate at Marmo in Bristol. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘We were chatting as soon as we sat down’
standfirst: Jacob, 27, a volunteer manager, meets Sophie, 28, a journalist
trailText: Jacob, 27, a volunteer manager, meets Sophie, 28, a journalist
body:
Jacob on Sophie

What were you hoping for?
To meet someone who I could connect with and possibly go on further dates.

First impressions?
Sophie was very nice and upbeat.

What did you talk about?
Our conversation went all over the place, from both of us having connections to the US to her organising standup comedy nights.

Most awkward moment?
There were a couple of moments where the conversation stalled, but overall it flowed nicely.

Good table manners?
Yes.

Best thing about Sophie?
She was very funny and had me laughing out loud.

Would you introduce Sophie to your friends?
I don’t think we are at that stage.

Describe Sophie in three words
Kind, authentic, humorous.

What do you think Sophie made of you?
I have no idea but I hope she enjoyed our conversation.

Did you go on somewhere?
No.

And … did you kiss?
No.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
I would have not arrived 15 minutes early. Multiple readings of a menu that I had already looked at online could have been avoided.

Marks out of 10?
7. She was a lovely person and I really enjoyed my time with her.

Would you meet again?
I enjoyed the evening but if we were to meet up again, it would be as friends.

Sophie on Jacob

What were you hoping for?
To meet someone interesting, kind and fun.

First impressions?
Super easy to talk to from the get-go. We were chatting as soon as we sat down.

What did you talk about?
Why neither of us lives in the US any more. Being “Jew-ish”. How Londoners get a bad reputation (the city is more inviting than people think).

Most awkward moment?
Probably when we were leaving. I had to go on elsewhere, so we parted ways a bit abruptly.

Good table manners?
Very.

Best thing about Jacob?
He is really kind and genuine. He cares a lot about doing good in the world, and I find it admirable that he moved to London on somewhat of a whim.

Would you introduce Jacob to your friends?
He’s travelled a lot, so his geographic knowledge could come in handy at a pub quiz.

Describe Jacob in three words
Friendly, kind, open.

What do you think Jacob made of you?
Hopefully he thought I was funny!

Related: Blind date: ‘I made him take a few too many selfies…’

Did you go on somewhere?
No, unfortunately we were going in different directions.

And … did you kiss?
Just a hug.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
If I hadn’t made plans, we could have chatted for a little longer, or at least walked to the tube together.

Marks out of 10?
8.

Would you meet again?
As friends.

Jacob and Sophie ate at Galvin Bistrot and Bar, London E1. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘We swapped numbers. I think that sends out good vibes, no?’
standfirst: Hugh, 55, a teacher and musician, meets Edie, 50, an independent advocate
trailText: Hugh, 55, a teacher and musician, meets Edie, 50, an independent advocate
body:
Hugh on Edie

What were you hoping for?
An exciting, exhilarating experience and a beautiful lady to talk to.

First impressions?
When she arrived, on time, I thought she looked stunning, and when we started to talk the conversation just flowed. We seemed to click straight away.

What did you talk about?
Our backgrounds and family. Music. Food. But for me, the best surprise was that she speaks Catalan, my mother tongue!

Most awkward moment?
It was definitely waiting for her arrival. I was a bit early and ordered myself a negroni to settle the nerves.

Good table manners?
Brilliant.

Best thing about Edie?
She laughed a lot, and I liked the way her face lit up.

Would you introduce Edie to your friends?
Definitely, she is fun and a good craic!

Describe Edie in three words.
Glorious, exciting, admirable.

What do you think Edie made of you?
We swapped numbers: I think that sends out good vibes, no?

Did you go on somewhere?
She gave me a lift to where I was staying …

And … did you kiss?
We hugged … Never say never!

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
That it had lasted longer. The food was sensational, the company too. Does that sound a bit cheesy?

Marks out of 10?
A solid 10.

Would you meet again?
Yes, 100%.

Edie on Hugh

What were you hoping for?
Someone who was easy to talk to and funny. Anything else would be a bonus.

First impressions?
I nearly jumped out of my skin when he shouted “Are you Edie?” before I was through the door of the restaurant. He was smiley, friendly and relaxed.

What did you talk about?
Births, deaths and marriages. A shared love of Catalunya. Music. Instruments. My puppy named Peter. Family.

Most awkward moment?
A huge cheese plant next to him kept covering his head as he was talking. We decided to name her (Kitty) and let her join the date.

Good table manners?
We spent the evening competing for best table manners.

Best thing about Hugh?
He doesn’t take himself too seriously, which gives a good vibe.

Would you introduce Hugh to your friends?
Of course. They would find him funny.

Describe Hugh in three words.
Funny, interesting, relaxed.

What do you think Hugh made of you?
I think he was a little disappointed I wasn’t as passionate about bands/music as him. He kept coming back to music and asking me questions about bands, and I think I got the answers wrong.

Related: Blind date: ‘She seemed to like me, but I’ve been wrong about this kind of thing before’

Did you go on somewhere?
We stayed until the restaurant closed as we were chatting away. He asked me to give him a lift to where he was staying, which I found a little awkward. I felt put on the spot.

And … did you kiss?
We had a two-cheek European kiss and said, “Bona nit”.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
Nothing.

Marks out of 10?
A solid 8.

Would you meet again?
Sure, but on a friendship level.

Hugh and Edie ate at Bar Etna in Altrincham. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘I should have made a move, but I’m not good at that sort of thing’
standfirst: Suli, 25, an animation graduate, meets Abigo, 26, a supervisor in retail
trailText: Suli, 25, an animation graduate, meets Abigo, 26, a supervisor in retail
body:
Suli on Abigo

What were you hoping for?
To meet someone I felt comfortable around and easy to talk to.

First impressions?
Abigo was funny and quite sure of herself.

What did you talk about?
Quite a lot: our creative sides, working in retail, mental health, family dynamics …

Most awkward moment?
I didn’t really feel awkward at any point after the first five minutes – and that was only nerves and me arriving a bit late. We had good chemistry.

Good table manners?
No complaints from me.

Best thing about Abigo?
I don’t think I can name just one: she was charming, confident, funny, intelligent, beautiful.

Would you introduce Abigo to your friends?
My friends are on a similar wavelength to me, so Abigo would be welcomed by them.

Describe Abigo in three words.
Feminist, influential, a diva.

What do you think Abigo made of you?
Laid-back, go with the flow, a sincere guy.

Did you go on somewhere?
We went to a park nearby to talk for a bit longer. She had an early train the next day, so we couldn’t stay too long.

And … did you kiss?
On the cheek, if that counts.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
I should have made a move, but I’m not good at that sort of thing. Otherwise it was a perfectly pleasant experience.

Marks out of 10?
9.

Would you meet again?
We are planning to go to the cinema soon.

Abigo on Suli

What were you hoping for?
To meet someone nice and interesting and eat some good food.

First impressions?
Super friendly and genuine. Couldn’t tell if he was nervous or just naturally a little reserved. He was dressed very well and was super polite.

What did you talk about?
Mental health. Dream jobs. School. Shoplifting. Music … and literally everything else. I had word vomit.

Most awkward moment?
He mentioned he has another date coming up. I could tell he felt awkward about being that honest, but I genuinely don’t think he knows how to lie or withhold information. It’s kind of cute.

Good table manners?
Great. We exchanged bites of steak.

Best thing about Suli?
He’s so easy to talk to, genuine and very down to earth. He has a very calming presence. And kind eyes. I told him that two minutes in.

Would you introduce Suli to your friends?
Absolutely. He would fit right in.

Describe Suli in three words.
Genuine, charming, layered.

What do you think Suli made of you?
Chatty, confident and medicated.

Related: Blind date: ‘I got a bit carried away once the wine kicked in’

Did you go on somewhere?
We sat in a park and talked.

And … did you kiss?
No.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
I would have liked to have gone on somewhere afterwards.

Marks out of 10?
10!

Would you meet again?
Yes.

Abigo and Suli ate at Gaucho in Manchester. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘I made him take a few too many selfies…’
standfirst: Lily, 26, a PhD student, meets Brodie, 24, a chef
trailText: Lily, 26, a PhD student, meets Brodie, 24, a chef
body:
Lily on Brodie

What were you hoping for?
Love, passion … marriage. Failing that, some good craic and a free dinner.

First impressions?
Very friendly and apologetic for being a little underdressed for the restaurant.

What did you talk about?
Our experiences working in hospitality and political canvassing. Our shared hatred of dating apps. How the restaurant gave us way too much food.

Most awkward moment?
I made him take a few too many selfies in case some of them turned out bad.

Good table manners?
Yes – “pleases” and “thank yous” to serving staff always go a long way.

Best thing about Brodie?
He seemed open to trying lots of new things and going with the flow of life. And he was happy to go along with all of my silly jokes.

Would you introduce Brodie to your friends?
I think they’d all get along very well. We had quite a lot in common.

Describe Brodie in three words.
Open, friendly and charming.

What do you think Brodie made of you?
Hopefully that I was funny and a good enough way to spend a Saturday night.

Did you go on somewhere?
No. We stayed in the restaurant until quite late, but my jet lag from a recent trip and the mountain of curry we ate caught up with me.

And … did you kiss?
No, just a friendly hug. I don’t think there was any romantic chemistry.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
Maybe the seating arrangement: morally, I am very against sitting elbow to elbow.

Marks out of 10?
7.

Would you meet again?
I don’t think so. Brodie was lovely and a great chat, but I was hoping for someone a bit older. Maybe I’ll see him out door-knocking at the next election.

Brodie on Lily

What were you hoping for?
Meet someone new without having to resort to Hinge; a laugh and a free meal.

First impressions?
Lily was a lot better dressed than me. And had an accent I couldn’t place.

What did you talk about?
Ceilidhs. The Green party. Talking to strangers. How fancy the restaurant was.

Most awkward moment?
Maybe when I said I thought she might be a Mancunian (she’s a Scouser).

Good table manners?
Yes, although neither of us knew which set of cutlery to use.

Best thing about Lily?
Lots of cool things going on in her life: studying; hobbies; moving around. Plus she had stayed in the wee village I lived in for a while, which was very wholesome.

Would you introduce Lily to your friends?
Why ever not!

Describe Lily in three words.
Clever, good selfie-taker, bold.

Related: Blind date: ‘Her one dating request was “no one in finance”. I work in finance’

What do you think Lily made of you?
Definitely similar in the no-spark type thing – always convenient when that’s mutual. Hopefully a bit interesting – and maybe a bit of a daydreamer.

Did you go on somewhere?
No.

And … did you kiss?
Also no.

If you could change one thing about the evening what would it be?
Less hay fever: I was fighting for my life half the evening. And next time I’ll check the place out on Google and dress a bit more accordingly.

Marks out of 10?
In a friendly rating, somewhere around 8. As a date, lower.

Would you meet again?
No, we’re quite different types of people. And I’m hoping to leave London asap, while Lily’s very happy here.

Lily and Brodie ate at Bombay Brasserie, London SW7. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘She seemed to like me, but I’ve been wrong about this kind of thing before’
standfirst: Philip, 74, an antiquarian book dealer, meets Carol, 66, who is retired
trailText: Philip, 74, an antiquarian book dealer, meets Carol, 66, who is retired
body:
Philip on Carol

What were you hoping for?
Reciprocated love at first sight (I don’t ask for much in this life). To meet a kindred spirit who might even become a partner.

First impressions?
We were both incredibly early, but caught the other’s eye and smiled. It was a nice moment.

What did you talk about?
Andy Burnham. Elvis Costello. Dogs. U3A groups. Trains to Italy. The deficiencies of dating apps. The pointlessness of shyness in later life.

Most awkward moment?
There weren’t any. Carol sent her G&T flying, but that was just funny, not awkward.

Good table manners?
Of course.

Best thing about Carol?
She’s fun to be with!

Would you introduce Carol to your friends?
Oh yes, they’d like her.

Describe Carol in three words
Warm, accomplished, quirky (I loved the little streak of pink in her hair).

What do you think Carol made of you?
I really don’t know, I’m not good at reading people. She seemed to like me, but I’ve been wrong about this kind of thing before.

Did you go on somewhere?
We linked arms until the parting of the ways.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
I wouldn’t change a thing.

And … did you kiss?
Not really, just a peck-on-the-cheek plus a hug.

Marks out of 10?
9.

Would you meet again?
Yes.

Carol on Philip

What were you hoping for?
An enjoyable evening, a tasty meal and great conversation. Someone to take a genuine interest in me as an individual.

First impressions?
He was smartly dressed, and had a kind face and a welcoming manner.

What did you talk about?
What life looks like as we get older. Our different careers. Ian McKellen – he who can do no wrong in my view.

Most awkward moment?
There were a few tiny missteps, but we took them in our stride.

Good table manners?
Excellent. Philip checked if I would be OK if he ordered steak tartare as a starter, and he was happy for me to share his salad.

Best thing about Philip?
Interesting and good conversationalist.

Would you introduce Philip to your friends?
I have a wide range of friends and he’d easily get along with some of them.

Related: Blind date: ‘Distance shouldn’t stand in the way of love … I did have to catch the last train home though’

Describe Philip in three words
Confident, curious, interesting.

What do you think Philip made of you?
I’d be happy with “easy to talk to”.

Did you go on somewhere?
No. Engineering works on my train line limited options.

And … did you kiss?
No.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
Not sure I would change anything.

Marks out of 10?
8.

Would you meet again?
We’ve swapped numbers.

Philip and Carol ate at Eataly London, EC2. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘I got a bit carried away once the wine kicked in’
standfirst: Alex, 45, a product lead in tech, meets Ellie, 35, a TV producer
trailText: Alex, 45, a product lead in tech, meets Ellie, 35, a TV producer
body:
Alex on Ellie

What were you hoping for?
To meet someone kind and have an enjoyable evening with someone I maybe wouldn’t ordinarily choose for myself.

First impressions?
Pretty, with great style, loads of personality and a really relaxed energy.

What did you talk about?
Work. Travelling. Shared Bristol connections and an unexpected link to a nightclub in Swindon. Her new personal training side hustle. Probably a bit too much about my cycling, in hindsight.

Most awkward moment?
I managed to make a bit of a mess with some crackers that were a lot more brittle than I expected.

Good table manners?
She had really nice table manners.

Best thing about Ellie?
Her smile and infectious laugh.

Would you introduce Ellie to your friends?
Absolutely.

Describe Ellie in three words
Warm, easygoing, fun.

What do you think Ellie made of you?
I’m not entirely sure. She was very honest at the end and said she didn’t feel romantic chemistry, which I respected. Aside from that, I hope she found me decent company.

Did you go on somewhere?
Nope.

And … did you kiss?
Only a friendly peck on the cheek.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
Probably I’d talk a little less. I think I got a bit carried away once the wine kicked in.

Marks out of 10?
7.5.

Would you meet again?
I’d definitely meet again as friends. I really enjoyed her company.

Ellie on Alex

What were you hoping for?
I try to have not to have too many expectations, but was hoping for good chat, laughter and alfresco dining.

First impressions?
We were both nervous and early, but as soon as I met him I was at ease.

What did you talk about?
Japan. Our lack of wine knowledge. Favourite fitness things.

Most awkward moment?
A piece of food fell out of my mouth as I was talking. But he nearly knocked his wine over, so I think we were even.

Good table manners?
Yes. Mine were worse, due to the above.

Best thing about Alex?
He has a really welcoming, warm vibe.

Would you introduce Alex to your friends?
Yes, but I can’t fully imagine us in each other’s social circles.

Describe Alex in three words
Warm, humble, intelligent.

What do you think Alex made of you?
I’m not sure. I think he agreed we had fun, but the attraction wasn’t there.

Related: Blind date: ‘It felt like taking part in Blind Date was a lifelong thing she wanted to do’

Did you go on somewhere?
No.

And … did you kiss?
Only the cheek.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
Some chemistry might have been nice.

Marks out of 10?
8.

Would you meet again?
I don’t think so, but I had a wonderful evening getting to know Alex.

Ellie and Alex ate at Pasta Ripiena in Bristol. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

headline: Blind date: ‘Her one dating request was “no one in finance”. I work in finance’
standfirst: Yusuf, 25, who works in finance, meets Hannah, 26, a PhD student
trailText: Yusuf, 25, who works in finance, meets Hannah, 26, a PhD student
body:
Yusuf on Hannah

What were you hoping for?
Someone interesting, good chat is more important than anything. And a fun story. I like a random side quest.

First impressions?
Great smile, really lovely northern accent – she seemed confident and excited.

What did you talk about?
Her Hackney half marathon. And her disdain for people in finance. “Not in finance” was her one date request (I work in finance).

Related: The pitfalls of dating on a school night

Most awkward moment?
Hannah said she thought I could be dyslexic five minutes in.

Good table manners?
Yep, no notes.

Best thing about Hannah?
Her accent, or her brains – she’s studying for a PhD.

Would you introduce Hannah to your friends?
My friends get on with most people, and the same is probably true for Hannah.

Describe Hannah in three words
Charismatic, clever and confident.

What do you think Hannah made of you?
Posh – she said. But hopefully good enough company for a Wednesday night.

Did you go on somewhere?
We were in the restaurant for nearly four hours! Late enough for a school night.

And … did you kiss?
Negative.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
Maybe more of a romantic spark.

Marks out of 10?
A solid 7 – lovely evening.

Would you meet again?
Absolutely, although probably as friends. Sounds like we’d do a cracking yoga class or something.

Hannah on Yusuf

What were you hoping for?
Low expectations, to be honest – my sister made me apply. But hopefully to go for a nice meal, meet someone random, and do something different on a Wednesday evening.

First impressions?
Really nice and friendly.

What did you talk about?
Jobs. Family. Writing these answers. Solo travel. Bank holiday plans.

Most awkward moment?
Maybe when he told me he worked in finance. I said I’d explicitly asked for someone who didn’t work in finance.

Good table manners?
Yes, although I was so focused on my own I didn’t pay much attention to his.

Best thing about Yusuf?
He was easy to chat to, asked questions and I felt comfortable straight away.

Related: Blind date: ‘I hope my handshake wasn’t too much of a red flag’

Would you introduce Yusuf to your friends?
Not sure how much they would have in common.

Describe Yusuf in three words
Interesting, friendly and chatty.

What do you think Yusuf made of you?
Probably that I talked a lot and was weird for saying I wasn’t a foodie.

Did you go on somewhere?
No, it was way past my bedtime.

And … did you kiss?
No.

If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
I can’t think of anything. I had a really nice time, but it was more as friends.

Marks out of 10?
8.

Would you meet again?
Potentially, as friends.

Yusuf and Hannah ate at the Bull & Last, London NW5. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com
